# My notes

A folder of plain text notes, indexed with notelight.

## Layout

Journal entries live in `journal/`, project notes in `projects/`, and old notes from the previous laptop in `legacy/`.

```sh
notelight index .
notelight search "how to back up"
```

# 2019

The year we planted the first garden.

# Sourdough log

Notes from a year of baking bread at home, kept so the next loaf is better than the last.

## Starter

The starter lives in the fridge and gets fed once a week: equal weights of flour and water, about 50 grams each. Before baking it needs two feeds at room temperature, twelve hours apart, until it doubles in four to six hours. A starter that smells of acetone is hungry, not dead.

## Hydration

Seventy percent hydration is forgiving: 700 grams of water for a kilogram of flour. Above 78 percent the dough spreads unless the flour is strong. Whole wheat drinks more water, so add five percent for every fifth of the flour that is whole grain.

## Bulk fermentation

Bulk fermentation took five hours at 24 degrees with four sets of stretch and folds in the first two hours. The dough is ready when it has grown by half, jiggles, and shows bubbles on the sides of the container. Under-proofed loaves have a tight, gummy crumb with a few large holes; over-proofed ones spread flat and taste sour.

## Baking

Bake in a preheated Dutch oven at 250 degrees, lid on for 20 minutes, then lid off at 230 degrees for another 25 until the crust is deep brown. Let it cool for an hour before cutting, or the crumb turns gummy.

## Troubleshooting

Flat loaf: weak shaping or over-proofing. Pale crust: oven not hot enough, or no steam. Dense crumb: the starter was not active, or bulk fermentation was cut short. Large tunnels under the crust: under-proofed, or the scoring was too shallow.

# Wednesday

Moved the backups to a second disk. The backup script copies the notes folder every night at two, keeps seven daily and four weekly snapshots, and emails me if a run fails.

## Reading

Finished the chapter on ownership and borrowing in the Rust book. A value has one owner; references borrow it, and the borrow checker makes sure no reference outlives the value.

# Thursday

Team meeting about the release: we agreed to ship the browser demo first and the npm package after it.

## Action items

- Write the changelog entry.
- Measure indexing speed in Chrome.
- Ask for a review before merging.

Café receipts from the trip to Lyon: 12€ for lunch, 4€ for coffee.

Remember the “bouchon” near the old town; best quenelles we had.

# Nested

Not ignored: an anchored pattern matches at the root.

# Shouting

Upper-case suffixes are still Markdown.

# Kept

Re-included by a negated pattern in .notelightignore.

# Garden plan

Tomatoes go in the sunny bed by the fence after the last frost, about mid May. Basil next to them; it likes the same warmth. Water deeply twice a week rather than a little every day.

## Compost

Turn the compost every two weeks. Brown material (leaves, cardboard) balances the green (kitchen scraps, grass); a heap that smells is too wet or too green.

Ideas for the browser app.

Keep the index in the origin private file system so it survives a reload, and fall back to IndexedDB where that is missing.

Embed only the chunks that changed: key the cache by the hash of the model id and the text, like the command line tool does.

Never upload a file. The only request is the model download, checked by SHA-256.

# Zebra

Upper-case Z sorts before lower-case letters.

# Apple

Lower-case a sorts after upper-case Z.

# Ärger

Non-ASCII names sort by code point, as in Python.
